 Order
Order No. 12.03.2025
 01. 1.
Heard learned counsel for the Petitioners and  learned counsel for the State.

2. The Petitioners are seeking pre-arrest bail in connection with G.R. Case No.44 of 2025, pending in the Court of learned J.M.F.C., Buguda, arising out of Buguda P.S. Case No.45 of 2025 for commission of alleged offences under Section 294, 313, 323, 376 (2) (n) 506, 34 I.P.C.
3.

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the Petitioners that admittedly the incident relates to the year 2017 for which an F.I.R has been instituted in 2025 and even if the recitals of the F.I.R is accepted at its face value, the principal accused is one Nilachal Sethy.
Hence, the Petitioners may be protected by pre-arrest bail.

sentences.text: 1 4. Learned counsel for the State opposes such prayer, inter alia, on the ground that there are allegations against the Petitioners in the statement under Section 183 of the BNSS and two of the co-accused have been taken into custody.
5. It is trite that merely because the co-accused have been taken into custody that does not act as embargo for considering the ABLAPL in respect of the other accused.

6. Considering the nature of allegations and the statement of the victim recorded under Section 183 of the Cr.P.C and that the present Petitioners are related to the principal accused, this Court directs that on surrendering within three weeks hence and moving for bail, the Petitioners shall be released on bail by the learned Court in seisin on such terms as deemed fit and proper.
7. Before releasing the learned Court shall verify as to whether this order has been assailed before the Apex Court and if so, the result thereof.
8. It is needless to state that the Petitioners shall cooperate with the ongoing investigation.
9. Accordingly, the ABLAPL stands disposed of.
(V. NARASINGH) Judge Soumya Signed by: SOUMYA RANJAN SAMAL
